docs.title: Lessons and Practical Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Always begin with Isti'adhah then Basmalah — before reciting Quran and before every action of life. This is a Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ and a Sunnah Allah established for all creation.

  2. Shaytan attacks through three channels — physical seizure (Hamz), temptation to arrogance (Nafkh), and subtle whispering (Nafth/Waswasah). Being aware of these channels helps the believer guard against them.

  3. Only Allah protects from Shaytan — no human effort or willpower alone can repel Shaytan's whisperings. Genuine protection requires turning to Allah.

  4. Bismillah is not limited to Quran recitation — it should precede all permissible actions: eating, drinking, sleeping, leaving the house, working. The hidden verb in the phrase signals this universality.

  5. Surah Al-Fatihah is the most comprehensive Surah — despite being only 7 short verses, it encapsulates the entire purpose of the Quran: creed, worship, legislation, guidance, and supplication.

  6. The Quran's arrangement is prophetically determined — the order of Surahs is not arbitrary. It was set by the Prophet ﷺ himself under divine guidance, which is why Surah Al-Fatihah — though not the first revealed — is placed first.

  7. Say Bismillah contrary to the idol worshippers — the Mushrikeen invoked their idols before actions. A Muslim's Bismillah is an act of Tawhid, distinguishing monotheism from polytheism in everyday life.

docs.title: Historical Context and Stories Mentioned
docs.text:
• Surah Al-Tawbah and the broken treaties: The Mushrikeen of Arabia violated their peace agreements with the Muslims. Allah revealed Surah Al-Tawbah expressing His wrath toward them. Because of the severity of this divine anger, the Surah opens without Bismillah — since Allah's mercy (expressed in الرحمن الرحيم) cannot be joined with His wrath in the same opening.

  • Ubayy ibn Ka'b رضي الله عنه recited Surah Al-Fatihah before the Prophet ﷺ, who testified it is unmatched by anything revealed in the Tawrah, Injil, Zabur, or Quran.

  • Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla رضي الله عنه was promised by the Prophet ﷺ that he would be taught the greatest Surah in the Quran — which is Surah Al-Fatihah.

  • Prophet ﷺ's Tahajjud practice: He would wake at night, begin prayer with Takbir, then recite the extended Isti'adhah: أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم من همزه ونفخه ونفثه.

  • Imam Al-Tabari رحمه الله is cited: Allah taught the Prophet ﷺ to mention His Names before all actions and made this a universal Sunnah and path (سبيلاً يتبعونه) for all of creation.

  • Imam Al-Qurtubi رحمه الله counted the names of Surah Al-Fatihah and reached 12 distinct names.

docs.title: Q&A Highlights
docs.text:
Q: Should we buy a large Quran with margins to write commentary alongside the text? A: The teacher (Dr. Asghar Mahmood Nadawi) clarified this is not necessary. The book Safwat al-Tafasir is the primary text. Students should take personal notes in a notebook during the lesson. What the teacher explains orally should be recorded in one's own notebook — that is sufficient.

Q: Why is the verb hidden in Bismillah, and why does the phrase start with a Haar Majroor (جار ومجرور)? A: In Arabic rhetoric (البلاغة), verbs are sometimes omitted deliberately. In Bismillah, the verb is hidden because the phrase applies to all activities of life — not just one act. If a specific verb were stated (e.g., أقرأ — I recite), it would restrict Bismillah to recitation only. By leaving the verb unmentioned, it encompasses eating, sleeping, going out, and every other action. This is the rhetorical wisdom (حكمة بلاغية) behind the omission. The sentence is a verbal sentence (جملة فعلية) with a hidden verb.

Note on next session: The class will begin from the Tafsir portion, page 25 of Safwat al-Tafasir. Students are to come prepared and divide the reading of the Tafsir section among themselves (4–5 lines per student). The language/vocabulary section within the book will be covered contextually during the Tafsir explanation, not separately.

docs.title: Tafseer 201 - Study Notes
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-06 Surah Covered: Surah Al-Fatiha (complete — all seven ayat)

docs.title: Session Overview
docs.text: This session completed the tafseer of Surah Al-Fatiha, covering all seven ayat in sequence. The teacher explained the Arabic vocabulary, grammatical structure (i'rab), and deeper meanings of each phrase, drawing on classical tafseer texts and hadith. The session also included a Q&A on the distinction between Al-Maghdubi Alayhim and Al-Dallin, practical guidance on reciting Al-Fatiha with presence of mind (khushu'), and administrative notes on classroom expectations for future lessons (Surah Al-Baqarah beginning next class).

docs.title: Key Themes and Topics
docs.text:
1. Hamd and Thana (Praise and Thanks) — Allah SWT taught humanity the correct formula for praising and thanking Him: Alhamdulillah.
  2. Allah's Sifat (Attributes) — The ayat of Al-Fatiha are a sequence of Allah's attributes: Rabb, Al-Rahman, Al-Rahim, Malik — each in the genitive (majrur) case as sifat linked to Lillahi.
  3. The Mercy of Allah (Rahmah) — Al-Rahman and Al-Rahim as Ism al-Mubalagha and Sifat al-Mushabbaha indicating the highest degree of mercy; the famous hadith that 1% of Allah's mercy is manifest in this world, 99% reserved for the Day of Judgment.
  4. Tawhid in Worship and Reliance — Iyyaka Na'budu wa Iyyaka Nasta'in: singling out Allah alone for worship (ibadah) and seeking help (isti'anah).
  5. The Straight Path and Its People — Sirat al-Mustaqeem identified as the way of the Anbiya, Siddiqeen, Shuhada, and Salihin (referenced from Surah An-Nisa).
  6. Two Groups of Deviation — Al-Maghdubi Alayhim (those upon whom is Allah's wrath, primarily the Jews) and Al-Dallin (those who went astray, primarily the Christians), and why each designation applies to each group.
  7. Practical Recitation with Meaning — The teacher's emphasis on repeating ayat during salah with their meanings actively in mind, especially in voluntary (nafl) prayers.

docs.title: Important Vocabulary
docs.text: Arabic Term Meaning حَمِدَ يَحْمَدُ حَمْدًا To praise someone اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ All praise is due to Allah رَبٌّ Sustainer, Lord, Nurturer عَالَمٌ (pl. عَالَمُونَ / عَالَمِينَ) World; a category of creation (Jama' Muzakkar Salim plural) اِسْمُ الْجِنْسِ Common noun (used here for عَالَمٌ — it covers all categories of worlds) شُكْرٌ Gratitude, thanks ثَنَاءٌ Praise, eulogy إِحْسَانٌ Goodness, benevolence, kindness جَمِيلٌ Kindness (synonym of إحسان) إِيجَادٌ Bringing into existence (from عَدَمٌ — nothingness) اَلرَّحْمَنُ The Most Gracious — highest degree of mercy (Ism al-Mubalagha) اَلرَّحِيمُ The Most Merciful — established, continuous mercy (Sifat al-Mushabbaha) اِسْمُ الْمُبَالَغَةِ Noun of exaggeration/intensification — indicates the highest level of a quality صِفَةٌ مُشَبَّهَةٌ Resembling adjective — indicates a stable, continuous attribute وَسِعَتْ رَحْمَتُهُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ His mercy encompasses all things دَائِمُ الْإِحْسَانِ Ever-benevolent, eternally kind سَعَادَةُ الدَّارَيْنِ Happiness of both worlds (dunya and akhirah) مَالِكٌ (Ism al-Fa'il) Owner, possessor يَوْمُ الدِّينِ Day of Recompense / Day of Judgment الدِّينُ Here: recompense, reward/punishment (root meaning: compensation) الْمُتَصَرِّفُ The One with full control/authority عِبَادَةٌ Worship (encompasses submission, humility, reverence) إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ You alone we worship (object pronoun placed first for exclusivity) إِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ You alone we seek help from نَخْضَعُ We submit, we bow down نَسْتَكِينُ We humble ourselves, we submit (from اِسْتَكَانَ يَسْتَكِينُ) نَخْشَعُ We feel humbleness/fear in the heart (خُشُوعٌ — awe from within) اِسْتِعَانَةٌ Seeking help (from عَوْنٌ — help; via استفعال pattern) عَوْنٌ Help, assistance أَعَانَ يُعِينُ To help اِسْتَعَانَ يَسْتَعِينُ To seek help إِهْدِنَا Guide us (amr / command form of هَدَى يَهْدِي هِدَايَةً) السِّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ The Straight Path (النعت / Sifat construction) ثَبَّتَنَا Make us steadfast/firm (تَثْبِيتًا — to make firm) الْمُقَرَّبُونَ Those close to Allah النَّبِيُّونَ The Prophets الصِّدِّيقُونَ The Truthful Ones / Foremost believers الشُّهَدَاءُ The Martyrs الصَّالِحُونَ The Righteous غَضِبَ يَغْضَبُ غَضَبًا To be angry الْمَغْضُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ Those upon whom is Allah's wrath ضَلَّ يَضِلُّ ضَلَالًا To go astray ضَالٌّ (pl. ضَالِّينَ) One who has gone astray (Ism Fa'il, Jama') جَهَالَةٌ / جَهَالَاتٌ Ignorance لُعِنَ Was cursed بَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ They brought upon themselves (Allah's) wrath

docs.title: Ayah 1 — اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
docs.text:
• Allah SWT Himself taught us the correct and worthy manner of praising Him by revealing this ayah. The command understood is: Qulu ya 'ibadi idha aradtum shukri wa thana'i: Alhamdulillah — "Say, O my servants, when you want to thank Me and praise Me: Alhamdulillah."
  • Alhamdulillah: All praise and thanks belong exclusively to Allah — not to any false deity or anything worshipped other than Him.
  • Rabb: Sustainer. This is a sifat (attribute) of Allah. He sustains all of creation.
  • Al-Alameen: Plural of 'Alam (world/category of creation). It is an ism al-jins (common noun) covering: the world of humans ('Alam al-Insan), world of Jinn ('Alam al-Jinn), world of Angels ('Alam al-Mala'ikah), world of animals ('Alam al-Haywanat), this world (dunya), and the next (akhirah).
  • Rabbul Alameen is one of the grammatical reasons the full phrase Lillahi Rabbil Alameen has kasra — all sifat here are majrur because they are linked to Lillahi.

docs.title: Ayah 2 — اَلرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
docs.text:
• Both Al-Rahman and Al-Rahim are sifat of Allah, both in the genitive (majrur) continuing the grammatical chain from Lillahi.
  • Al-Rahman: Ism al-Mubalagha — indicates the highest, most intense level of mercy.
  • Al-Rahim: Sifat al-Mushabbaha — indicates a continuous, established, permanent quality of mercy.
  • Meaning: Al-ladhi wasi'at rahmatuhu kulla shay'in — "He whose mercy encompasses all things."
  • Allah's mercy includes: creating us, providing sustenance (rizq), and guiding us to sa'adat al-darayn — happiness in both this world and the next.
  • Hadith point: All the mercy observable in this world — in human hearts, among animals, across all creation — constitutes only 1% of Allah's mercy. The remaining 99% will be released on the Day of Judgment. This underscores the meaning of Da'im al-Ihsan — Allah is ever-benevolent.
  • The verse wa in ta'uddu ni'mat Allahi la tuhsuha (Quran: "If you try to count Allah's blessings you cannot enumerate them") was cited to reinforce this point.

docs.title: Ayah 3 — مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
docs.text:
• Maliki: Owner, possessor — Ism al-Fa'il from malaka.
  • Yawm al-Din: The Day of Recompense. Din here means compensation/reward — the day on which every person will be given the recompense for their deeds (reward for good, punishment for evil).
  • Allah is al-Mutasarrif fi Yawm al-Din — He has complete, unrestricted authority on that day, as an owner (malik) has over his own dominion (mulk).
  • In dunya, Allah gives people relative control as a test — do they think they are the true owners, or do they acknowledge Allah's ownership? On the Day of Judgment, even that relative human control is removed.
  • Supporting ayah: Yawma la tamliku nafsun linafsin shay'an wal amru yawma idhin lillah — "On that day no soul shall have power to do anything for another, and all authority will belong to Allah."

docs.title: Ayah 4 — إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
docs.text:
• The pronoun Iyyaka (You alone) is placed before the verb — in Arabic this indicates hasr (exclusivity/restriction). The meaning: "You, and only You, we worship."
  • Ibadah encompasses: nakhda'u (submission), nastakinu (humbling of the self), nakhsha'u (feeling awe and fear in the heart — khushu').
  • We single out (nakhussu) Allah alone for worship: La na'budu ahadan siwak — "We worship no one except You."
  • Isti'anah (seeking help): from 'Awn (help) via the istif'al pattern, meaning to seek/request help. Iyyaka nasta'in = "Only from You do we seek help."
  • We need Allah's help specifically to worship Him, to obey Him, and to please Him — because He alone has the power to enable us and accept our worship.
  • La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah is the spirit of this ayah.

docs.title: Ayah 5 — اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
docs.text:
• Ihdi: Command form (amr) of hada yahdi hidayatan — to guide, to show the path.
  • Al-Sirat al-Mustaqeem: The straight, upright, exact and true path — a Na't Sifat construction.
  • The full du'a meaning: "O Allah, guide us, make us steadfast (thabbitna) upon Islam — the Islam with which You sent Your Prophets and Messengers, and the final Messenger (Khatam al-Mursaleen)."
  • Make us among al-muqarrabin — those closest to Allah.

docs.title: Ayah 6 — صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ
docs.text:
• This ayah defines who treads Al-Sirat al-Mustaqeem — those upon whom Allah has bestowed His bounty (ni'mah).
  • These are identified from Surah An-Nisa (fifth juz): "Ula'ika alladhina an'ama Allahu alayhim min al-Nabiyyina wa al-Siddiqina wa al-Shuhada'i wa al-Salihin"
  • Al-Nabiyyun: The Prophets of Allah
  • Al-Siddiqun: The foremost truthful followers of the Prophets (e.g., Abu Bakr al-Siddiq — the first and foremost follower of the Prophet SAW, who attained the rank of Siddiqiyyah)
  • Al-Shuhada': Those who attained martyrdom in the way of Allah
  • Al-Salihin: All righteous people
  • These four groups are together in Jannah: "wa hasuna ula'ika rafiqa" — "and what excellent companions they are."
  • Every believer in every raka'ah of every salah is making this supplication — asking Allah to be placed on the way of the Anbiya, Siddiqeen, Shuhada, and Salihin. This is profound.

docs.title: Ayah 7 — غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
docs.text:
• A prayer for protection from two deviated groups.
  • Al-Maghdubi Alayhim — Those upon whom is Allah's wrath: primarily the Jews (Yahud).
  • Reason: They deviated from the right way knowingly and deliberately despite having many Prophets sent to them and having full knowledge of the truth.
  • Quranic evidence: "Lu'ina alladhina kafaru min Bani Isra'il 'ala lisan Dawuda wa 'Isa ibn Maryam" and "ba'u bi ghadabin min Allah." The words ghadab, la'nah, and maghdub are specifically used for the Jews in multiple Quranic ayat.
  • Hadith also specifically interprets Al-Maghdubi Alayhim as referring to the Jews.
  • Al-Dallin — Those who have gone astray: primarily the Christians (Nasara).
  • Reason: They deviated from the right way due to ignorance and distance from the actual teachings of 'Isa AS. After 'Isa AS departed and before the coming of the Prophet Muhammad SAW, they lost connection with the true teachings and went astray.
  • The word Dallin (from dalla yadillu dalalan) indicates straying/being lost, as opposed to willful defiance.
  • Important clarification (Q&A): These two groups are specifically named because they represent the most prominent examples — but all forms of deviation are included in these two ayat. Mushrikeen (polytheists), atheists, and all others who deviate from the straight path are encompassed in the meaning. The ayah does not name Jews and Christians explicitly — Allah left it general — but classical scholars and hadith identify these two groups as the primary referents.
  • The full du'a meaning: "Allahumma la taj'alna ya Allah min zumrati a'da'ik al-ha'idina 'an al-sirat al-mustaqim" — "O Allah, do not make us from the group of Your enemies who deviate from the Straight Path."
  • We close with Ameen — affirming and requesting acceptance of this entire supplication.

docs.title: Grammar and Language Notes
docs.text:
• I'rab chain in Al-Fatiha: Lillahi → Rabbil Alameen → Al-Rahmani Al-Rahimi → Maliki Yawm al-Din: all are majrur (genitive) because they are sifat linked to the majrur word Lillahi (harf al-jar = Lam). Each subsequent sifat carries the same kasra.
  • عَالَمُونَ / عَالَمِينَ: Plural of 'Alam; the plural form used is Jama' Muzakkar Salim (sound masculine plural).
  • اِسْمُ الْمُبَالَغَةِ vs. صِفَةٌ مُشَبَّهَةٌ: Al-Rahman is Ism al-Mubalagha (superlative intensity of mercy). Al-Rahim is Sifat Mushabbaha (settled, continuous attribute of mercy). Both indicate the highest levels of the root meaning rahima.
  • مَالِكٌ: Ism al-Fa'il (active participle) from malaka yamliku.
  • إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ: The object pronoun (Iyyaka) precedes the verb (na'budu) — this fronting (taqdim) in Arabic grammar signals hasr (restriction/exclusivity): worship is restricted to Allah alone.
  • اِسْتَعَانَ: Istif'al pattern from 'Awn. In the istif'al pattern, the meaning is always "to seek/request" the base action. So ista'ana = to seek help.
  • ضَالٌّ (pl. ضَالِّينَ): Ism al-Fa'il from dalla yadillu dalalan; the plural Dallin is used in the ayah.
  • Student note-taking guidance from teacher: When studying Quranic words, know: (1) root word, (2) plural if applicable, (3) if a verb — its madhi, mudhari', and which bab it belongs to, (4) the exact Quranic/Arabic meaning.

docs.title: Lessons and Practical Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Recite Al-Fatiha with meaning: The teacher strongly emphasized that we should actively hold the meanings of each ayah in our mind while reciting, especially in nafl (voluntary) prayers. For instance, while saying Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim, consciously reflect on all forms of mercy — Allah's mercy in creation, in provision, in guidance — and how 99% of that mercy is yet to be unveiled.

  2. Repeat ayat in reflection: It is established from hadith that the Prophet SAW would repeat an ayah again and again — if it was an ayah about Jannah, he would repeat it with longing; if about Jahannam, with fear and seeking refuge. We should do the same, particularly in nafl prayers. This is permissible and praiseworthy.

  3. Understand the weight of Maliki Yawm al-Din: Reciting this ayah should bring to mind the reality of the Day of Judgment — a day on which no soul can help another, and all authority belongs to Allah alone. This should produce humility, urgency, and motivation for good deeds.

  4. The salah as a recurring supplication: Every single raka'ah of prayer contains this complete du'a. We are asking Allah, repeatedly every day, to put us on the path of the Anbiya, Siddiqeen, Shuhada, and Salihin — and to protect us from the path of those who earned Allah's wrath or went astray. We must be conscious of what we are asking.

  5. Differentiate khushu' from mere movement: Nakhsha'u means internal humility and awe — a feeling in the heart, not just physical posture. This is the goal of salah.

  6. Gratitude is a duty: Allah has bestowed blessings we cannot count (wa in ta'uddu ni'mat Allahi la tuhsuha). The response to this is constant hamd and shukr — which is itself taught to us by Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen.

  7. Preparation for class: Students are expected to prepare the tafseer portion of each lesson before the class and practice reading the Arabic ibarah with correct recitation. For Surah Al-Baqarah (beginning next class), come having read the baina yaday al-surah (introduction to the surah) and the tafseer text.

docs.title: Historical Context and Stories Mentioned
docs.text:
• The Jews (Bani Isra'il): Allah sent an exceptionally large number of Prophets to Bani Isra'il, yet they repeatedly and knowingly disobeyed. This persistent, deliberate deviation is why the Quran associates ghadab (wrath) and la'nah (curse) with them in numerous ayat. Reference: "Lu'ina alladhina kafaru min Bani Isra'il 'ala lisan Dawuda wa 'Isa ibn Maryam" — the curse came through the tongues of two of their own Prophets (Dawud AS and 'Isa AS), indicating the severity of their transgression.

  • The Christians (Nasara): After the departure of 'Isa AS, a long period elapsed before the coming of Prophet Muhammad SAW. During this interval, the Christians gradually lost connection with the authentic teachings of 'Isa AS — through ignorance, neglect, and the corruption of their scriptures. This is distinguished from the Jews' case of willful rejection: the Christians' deviation was rooted more in jahalah (ignorance) and distance from the original message.

  • Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA): Mentioned as the prime example of a Siddiq — the first and foremost in following and believing the Prophet SAW, attaining the rank of Siddiqiyyah through his truthfulness and immediate acceptance of truth.

  • Hadith on Allah's Mercy: The Prophet SAW stated that Allah divided His mercy into 100 parts — He sent down 1 part to this world, and by that 1 part all of creation shows mercy to one another (mother to child, animal to its young, etc.). The remaining 99 parts are reserved for the believers on the Day of Judgment. (Referenced from Sahih Bukhari and Muslim.)

docs.title: Q&A Highlights
docs.text:
Q: What are the differences between نَخْضَعُ, نَسْتَكِينُ, and نَخْشَعُ? A: All three are synonyms related to worship and humility, but can be differentiated: - Nakhda'u (خَضَعَ) — to submit, to bow down - Nastakinu (اِسْتَكَانَ يَسْتَكِينُ) — to humble oneself, to submit completely - Nakhsha'u (خَشَعَ يَخْشَعُ) — to feel internal humbleness and awe in the heart before Allah (khushu' is the noun). This is the inward, spiritual dimension of ibadah.

Q: Do Al-Maghdubi Alayhim and Al-Dallin only refer to Jews and Christians, or do they include atheists and polytheists too? A: All forms of deviation are included in the broad meaning of these two ayat — mushrikeen, atheists, and all who stray are encompassed. However, classical scholars and the hadith of the Prophet SAW specifically interpret Al-Maghdubi Alayhim as the Jews and Al-Dallin as the Christians, because these are the highest and most prominent examples: the Jews' deviation was willful and knowledgeable, and the Christians' was due to ignorance and neglect. The ayah deliberately leaves the names out so the meaning remains universal and comprehensive.

Q: Why specifically is Maghdub (wrath) used for Jews and Dallin (straying) for Christians? A: Because the Quran itself uses ghadab and la'nah specifically in connection with the Jews in multiple places (e.g., Surah Al-Ma'idah), and hadith confirm this interpretation. The Jews knew the truth and rejected it deliberately — hence wrath (an active divine response to willful transgression). The Christians lost the truth through ignorance and neglect of 'Isa AS's actual teachings — hence straying (a passive condition of being lost rather than actively defiant).

Q: Is it permissible to write on a Quran that has blank lines (for annotation/tafseer notes)? A: The teacher clarified that the class tafseer book already contains the Quranic text with tafseer explanations. Students should record everything in their personal notebooks — especially the Arabic words, meanings, and grammatical analysis. The blank-lined Quran is only the Quranic text without tafseer, so the class book and notebook are the primary tools.

Q: Is it permissible to repeat a single ayah multiple times during salah? A: Yes. It is established (ja'iz) from the sunnah — the Prophet SAW would stop at ayat mentioning Jannah and repeat them with longing, and at ayat mentioning Jahannam and repeat them while seeking refuge. In nafl prayers especially, repeating individual ayat while reflecting on their meaning is encouraged. In fard prayers in jama'ah, this is less practical since others are present, but in individual nafl prayers there is no restriction.

Q: What will be covered next class? A: Surah Al-Baqarah begins next class, starting with Baina Yaday al-Surah (the introduction to the surah). Students should come having prepared the tafseer portion of the lesson beforehand.

docs.title: Tafseer 201 - Study Notes
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-13 Surah Covered: Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 3–7 (Page 32 of the tafseer text)

docs.title: Session Overview
docs.text: This session continued the tafseer of Surah Al-Baqarah, focusing on the remaining qualities of the Muttaqeen (the God-fearing) described in Ayat 3–5, followed by an introduction to Ayat 6–7 concerning the disbelievers (Kuffar). The sheikh read and explained the Arabic text of the tafseer book directly, with students participating in reading. Key qualities covered included belief in the Unseen (Iman bil Ghayb), establishment of Salah (Iqamatus Salah), spending from provisions (Infaq), belief in revealed scriptures, and belief in the Hereafter. The session concluded partway through Ayah 7, with the full explanation of Khatamallahu deferred to the next class.

docs.title: Key Themes and Topics
docs.text:
1. The qualities of the Muttaqeen — five attributes enumerated across Ayat 3–5
  2. Iman bil Ghayb — believing in what cannot be perceived through the senses
  3. Iqamatus Salah — what it truly means to "establish" prayer (not merely perform it)
  4. Infaq and Zakat — the scope of spending: obligatory vs. voluntary; Ibn Jarir vs. Ibn Abbas on the ayah's range
  5. Belief in all divine scriptures and all prophets — without differentiation
  6. Yaqeen in the Akhirah — the higher degree of certainty required for belief in the Hereafter
  7. Munasabah (contextual link) — why the Quran pairs descriptions of believers with descriptions of disbelievers
  8. The Kuffar's sealed hearts — the reason their Iman cannot enter (Khatamallahu ala qulubihim)
  9. Consolation to the Prophet ﷺ — the pedagogical function of Ayah 6

docs.title: Important Vocabulary
docs.text: Arabic Term Meaning الغيب (al-Ghayb) The Unseen; things absent from the senses; used here as a theological term for matters of creed يُؤمِنون (yu'minoon) They believe; from أَمَنَ (amana) الحَوَاسّ (al-Hawass) The sense organs (hearing, sight, touch, etc.) إقامة الصلاة (Iqamatus Salah) Establishing/maintaining prayer in its most complete form إتمام (itmam) Completion; fulfilling something in full الخشوع (al-Khushu') Humility and submissiveness in prayer يُؤدّونها (yu'adduunaha) They perform/fulfill it (the prayer); from أَدَّى يُؤَدِّي رَزَقَ (razaqa) To provide; رَزَقناهم = what We have provided them يُنفِقون (yunfiqoon) They spend (in the way of Allah) الزكاة (az-Zakat) Obligatory almsgiving الصدقات (as-Sadaqat) Voluntary charity/charities اختيار (ikhtiyar) Choice, selection (of an interpretive opinion); اختار = he chose/selected اليقين (al-Yaqeen) Certain, firm belief; a higher level than Iman أَيقَنَ يُوقِنُ إِيقاناً (ayqana yuqinu iqanan) To be certain, to have firm conviction; Form IV verb اعتقاداً جازماً (i'tiqadan jaziman) A firm/decisive belief (without doubt) الآخرة (al-Akhirah) The Hereafter; the next abode; named so because it comes after (ba'd) this world أُولئك (ula'ika) Those (people); referring to the Muttaqeen المفلحون (al-Muflihoon) The truly successful ones; those who attain final victory المناسبة (al-Munasabah) The contextual link/connection between successive sets of ayat الأبرار (al-Abrar) The righteous, the good-doers الفجّار (al-Fujjar) The wicked, the evil-doers أهل السعادة (Ahl as-Sa'adah) The fortunate people أهل الشقاوة (Ahl ash-Shaqawah) The unfortunate people إنّ (inna) Indeed; verily; conveys certainty/emphasis جَحَدَ (jahada) To deny, to reject outright سواء (sawa') Equal; the same أنذَرَ يُنذِرُ إنذاراً (andhara yundhiru indharan) To warn; give a warning; نذير = one who warns لا يُؤمِنون (la yu'minoon) They will not believe تسلية (tasliyah) Comfort, consolation خَتَمَ يَختِمُ خَتماً (khatama yakhtim khatman) To seal; to put a seal on something خاتَم المرسَلين (Khatamul Mursaleen) The seal of the messengers (a title of the Prophet ﷺ) العلّة (al-'illah) The reason, the cause

docs.title: Ayah 3 — The Three Qualities of the Muttaqeen
docs.text:
1. الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ — Those who believe in the Unseen

  • Ghayb here is a theological/creedal term, not merely "absence."
  • It refers to everything that cannot be perceived through the five senses.
  • Examples: the Resurrection (al-Ba'th), Paradise (al-Jannah), Hellfire (an-Nar), the Bridge (as-Sirat), the Reckoning (al-Hisab), and everything else the Quran and the Prophet ﷺ have informed us of.
  • We affirm these things not by sense-experience but by the testimony of Allah and His Messenger.

2. وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ — And they establish the prayer

  • Iqamatus Salah means performing the prayer in the most complete and perfect manner — not merely going through the motions.
  • This includes:
  • Fulfilling all conditions (shurut) of prayer
  • Completing all pillars (arkan) of prayer
  • Maintaining khushu' (humility and submissiveness)
  • Observing the etiquettes (adab) of prayer
  • Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) explained iqamatuha as: completing the ruku' (bowing), sujud (prostration), tilawah (recitation), and khushu' (humility).
  • Other mufassiroon extended the meaning further: managing the mosque, calling people to prayer, and organizing all affairs related to salah — all fall under "establishing" it.

3. وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ — And they spend from what We have provided them

  • Razaqnahum = what We have given them (money, provisions, property).
  • Yunfiqoon = they spend from it; they give charity in all good and virtuous ways (fi wujuhil khayr wal ihsan).
  • The ayah is general ('ammah) — it encompasses all forms of giving.
  • Scholarly difference on the scope:
  • Ibn Jarir at-Tabari (رحمه الله): chose the view that the ayah includes all types of spending — obligatory Zakat, voluntary Sadaqah, and all other charitable expenditures.
  • Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه): understood the ayah to refer specifically to the obligatory Zakat al-Amwal only.
  • Ibn Kathir (رحمه الله): both the obligatory expenses (nafaqat wajibah) and the obligatory Zakat are included in this ayah. He notes that both Fard and Wajib giving fall under الَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ.

Why does Allah frequently pair Salah and Infaq?

Ibn Kathir (رحمه الله) explains: - As-Salah is the right of Allah (haqqullah); it contains tawhid, glorification (tamjid), and praise (thana') of Allah. - Al-Infaq is the right of the people/creation (haqqul makhluq); it expresses kindness (ihsan) toward the creations of Allah. - Together they represent the two fundamental axes of Islamic conduct: fulfilling one's duty to God and to fellow creation. This pairing appears throughout the Quran (e.g., أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ).

docs.title: Ayah 4 — Two Further Qualities
docs.text:
4. وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ And those who believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you

  • Bima unzila ilayka = the Holy Quran.
  • Wa ma unzila min qablika = the earlier divine scriptures: the Torah (Tawrah), the Gospel (Injil), the Psalms (Zabur), and all other books revealed to previous prophets.
  • Belief is in these books in their original, unaltered form — not the distorted, amended versions that exist today.
  • The Muttaqeen do not differentiate between the books of Allah (la yufarriqoona bayna Kutubillah) nor between His messengers (wa la bayna Rusulihi).
  • This distinguishes the believer from Jews and Christians, who accept only their own prophet and reject others. Muslims believe in all prophets and all books.

5. وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ — And in the Hereafter they have certainty (Yaqeen)

  • Yuqinoon from أَيقَنَ يُوقِنُ إِيقاناً — a firm, decisive belief.
  • Meaning: ya'taqidoona i'tiqadan jaziman la yulabisahu shakkun aw irtiyab — a firm belief without any doubt or suspicion.
  • Belief in the Hereafter includes all related matters: the Resurrection, the reward and punishment, the Balance (al-Mizan), and all that follows.
  • Why was Yaqeen used for the Akhirah rather than Iman?
  • Iman covers the beginning stages of belief through its various increasing levels.
  • Yaqeen is the highest, most firm stage of belief — the final, settled level of certainty.
  • Iman has degrees; Yaqeen is the apex. Using Yaqeen for the Akhirah emphasizes that true belief in the Hereafter must reach this level of unshakeable conviction.
  • Why is it called "الآخرة"? Because it comes after (ba'd) this present world (ad-Dunya) — it is the final abode.

docs.title: Ayah 5 — The Outcome
docs.text:
أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.

  • Those characterized by the above five qualities receive huda (guidance) — a clear light and insight directly from Allah.
  • They are the Muflihoon — the truly successful. Falah here does not refer only to worldly success; it refers specifically to final, everlasting success in the Hereafter.
  • They attain the highest ranks in Jannah — this is the ultimate, permanent victory that cannot be taken away.

docs.title: Munasabah — Link to Ayat 6–7
docs.text:
The sheikh explained the munasabah (contextual connection) between the verses of the Muttaqeen (Ayat 1–5) and the verses about the Kuffar (Ayat 6–7):

  • After mentioning the qualities of believers, Allah follows with the qualities of disbelievers to make the distinction between the two groups clear (liyudhira al-fariq al-wadih bayna as-sinfayn).
  • This is a consistent method of the Quran: comparing the Abrar (righteous) with the Fujjar (wicked), and distinguishing Ahl as-Sa'adah (the fortunate) from Ahl ash-Shaqawah (the unfortunate).
  • An Arabic proverb captures the principle: بِضِدِّهَا تَتَمَيَّزُ الْأَشْيَاءُ — "By their opposites, things are distinguished."

docs.title: Ayah 6 — The Kuffar: Warning Makes No Difference
docs.text:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرُوهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ Indeed, those who disbelieve — it is equal to them whether you warn them or you do not warn them — they will not believe.

  • Al-ladhina kafaru = those who denied the ayat of Allah and rejected the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ.
  • Sawa'un alayhim = it is equal/the same for them.
  • Andhara yundhiru indharan = to warn; to give a warning.
  • Whether the Prophet ﷺ warned them from Allah's punishment and frightened them (khawwaftahum minhu), or did not warn them — in both cases: la yu'minoon — they will not believe.
  • This ayah is a consolation (tasliyah) to the Prophet ﷺ about the disbelief of his people. It does not mean he should stop inviting them; it means he should not grieve so much that it harms him. He has conveyed the message perfectly — their rejection is now their own responsibility.
  • Parallel examples from other prophets:
  • Nuh (عليه السلام): after exhausting all means of da'wah, supplicated: رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا — "O Lord, do not leave a single disbeliever on earth."
  • Musa (عليه السلام): supplicated: رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلَىٰ أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ — after performing all duties, when the prophet feels certain the people will not accept Iman.

docs.title: Ayah 7 — The Reason: Sealed Hearts (Begun, to be continued)
docs.text:
خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰ أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment.

  • Khatama = to seal; to place a seal. Same root as Khatamul Mursaleen (Seal of the Prophets).
  • Allah has sealed their hearts (qulubihim) — no light of Iman can enter; no faith illuminates within.
  • The reason (al-'illah) for their not believing is this seal — mentioned here to explain Ayah 6.
  • This section was not completed — the full explanation will continue in the next class.

docs.title: Grammar and Language Notes
docs.text:
• يُؤمِنون — from أَمَنَ (Form I); يُؤمِن is Form IV (أَفعَلَ).
  • يُؤدّونها — from أَدَّى يُؤَدِّي (Form II doubled); means "to perform/fulfill" — used for rendering something to its proper recipient in complete form.
  • يُوقِنون — from أَيقَنَ يُوقِنُ (Form IV: أَفعَلَ); madi: أَيقَنَ; mudari': يُوقِنُ; masdar: إِيقان. The sheikh asked students to identify this bab and form during class.
  • أُنزِلَ — passive form (fi'l majhul) of أَنزَلَ يُنزِلُ إِنزالاً (Form IV).
  • أَنذَرَ يُنذِرُ إِنذاراً — Form IV verb meaning "to warn"; the sheikh identified it as a transitive verb taking a direct object.
  • خَتَمَ يَختِمُ خَتماً — Form I verb meaning "to seal."
  • سَوَاءٌ — predicate adjective meaning "equal/the same"; here used in the structure sawa'un alayhim... am... = "it is equal to them whether... or..."
  • الزكاة المفروضة — al-Zakat al-mafrudah: mafrudah is a passive participle (Form I) meaning "what has been made obligatory/prescribed."
  • Arabic proverb taught: بِضِدِّهَا تَتَمَيَّزُ الْأَشْيَاءُ / تُعرَفُ الأشياءُ بأضدادِها — "Things are known/distinguished by their opposites."
  • مِن in mimma razaqnahum — partitive min (indicating "from/out of"), making infaq an act of spending from a portion of what one has, not all of it.

docs.title: Lessons and Practical Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Belief in the Unseen is the foundation — Iman in things we cannot see or touch is the first and most essential quality of a believer. Our creed does not rest on empirical proof alone but on the testimony of Allah and His Messenger.

  2. Salah must be "established," not merely "performed" — True iqamatus salah means fulfilling every condition, pillar, and etiquette with khushu'. A prayer done hastily or without focus does not meet the Quranic standard. Ibn Abbas specifically highlighted ruku', sujud, tilawah, and khushu' as its pillars of completion.

  3. Spending is an obligation, not an option — Infaq is listed alongside Salah as a defining quality of the Muttaqeen. Whether Fard Zakat or voluntary Sadaqah, giving in the way of Allah is central to Islamic identity.

  4. Salah = rights of Allah; Infaq = rights of creation — This is why they always appear together. A complete Muslim fulfills both: his vertical duty to Allah and his horizontal duty to people.

  5. Belief must not be selective — Accepting some prophets and rejecting others, or some books while rejecting others, is not valid Iman. Muslims believe in all prophets and all original scriptures without distinction.

  6. Yaqeen in the Akhirah should be our anchor — Our certainty about the Hereafter must be unshakeable — jazim (decisive), without doubt or suspicion. This firm conviction shapes behavior in this world.

  7. The da'i must not despair — The Prophet ﷺ was consoled that his duty is to convey, not to compel. A caller to Islam should not exhaust himself in grief over those who reject the message. Convey clearly, then leave the result to Allah.

  8. Contrast is a teaching tool — The Quran's method of pairing descriptions of believers and disbelievers side by side helps us see the stakes clearly and understand what is truly at risk. Studying both together deepens understanding of each.

  9. Hardened hearts are a consequence — The sealing of hearts in Ayah 7 is presented as the reason disbelievers cannot believe — a warning that persistent rejection can lead to a state where guidance no longer reaches the heart.

docs.title: Historical Context and Stories Mentioned
docs.text:
• Nuh (عليه السلام) — After exhausting every means of da'wah with his people over a very long time, he supplicated against them: رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا ("O Lord, leave not upon the earth any of the disbelievers"). This illustrates the stage a messenger reaches after fulfilling his duty completely and recognizing the people will not accept.

  • Musa (عليه السلام) — After Pharaoh's persistent rejection, Musa supplicated: رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلَىٰ أَمْوَالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُا الْعَذَابَ ("Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment"). The sheikh cited this as parallel to the situation addressed in Ayah 6 — the consolation to the Prophet ﷺ.

  • The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ — The ayah is understood as addressing his grief over the persistent rejection by the Quraysh and other disbelievers, assuring him he had fulfilled his prophetic duty and should not harm himself with excessive sorrow.

docs.title: Q&A Highlights
docs.text:
Q: What is the difference between Yaqeen (يقين) and Iman (إيمان)? Why did Allah use Yaqeen for the Akhirah and Iman for Ghayb?

A (Sheikh's explanation): Iman covers a spectrum — it starts from the beginning stages of belief and increases over time. It has multiple levels and degrees. Yaqeen is not a separate category but rather the highest, most firm level that Iman can reach — a settled, unshakeable conviction. So Iman is the broader term encompassing all stages, while Yaqeen is the apex of that journey. Allah used Yaqeen for the Akhirah because belief in the Hereafter — since it is the foundation of all moral accountability and the ultimate reality — must reach this highest degree of certainty. A general belief (the starting point of Iman) is not sufficient for something as weighty as the Akhirah; it must be firm, decisive, and free of all doubt.

Q (Clarification during reading): Is the word al-Zakat al-mafrudah in the genitive (majrur) form or is it a new sentence?

A: The sheikh clarified that min here is a partitive min, and al-Zakat al-mafrudah is a continuation of the sentence as the object (maf'ul bihi), not a new sentence.

docs.title: Tafseer 201 - Study Notes
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-18 Surah Covered: Surah Al-Baqarah — Ayahs 7–20 (focus on Ayah 7 and Ayahs 8–20, Munafiqeen section)

docs.title: Session Overview
docs.text: This session covered the tafseer of Surah Al-Baqarah, beginning with Ayah 7 (خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ — "Allah has sealed their hearts") and transitioning into the opening ayahs of the Munafiqeen section (Ayahs 8–20). The sheikh explained the theological meaning of the "sealing of the hearts," the three categories of people introduced in the surah's opening, the definition and characteristics of the Munafiqeen, the Sabab al-Nuzul (occasion of revelation) for the Munafiqeen ayahs, and began the detailed tafseer of Ayah 8 (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ). The session concluded with a discussion of Ayah 9 (يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ) before prayer time.

docs.title: Key Themes and Topics
docs.text:
1. Khatm al-Qulub (Sealing of the Hearts) — the meaning, mechanism, and cause of Allah sealing the hearts, ears, and eyesights of the disbelievers.
  2. Three Categories of Humanity — Mu'mineen, Kafireen, and Munafiqeen as the structural framework of Surah Al-Baqarah's opening.
  3. Al-Munasabah (Contextual Transition) — how the surah moves from qualities of believers → qualities of disbelievers → qualities of hypocrites.
  4. Definition and Danger of Nifaq — who the Munafiqeen are, what makes them the most dangerous and most hated group.
  5. Sabab al-Nuzul — the historical occasion behind the Munafiqeen ayahs, specifically named individuals.
  6. Tafseer of Ayah 8 — the verbal declaration of faith by hypocrites versus the reality of their hearts.
  7. Tafseer of Ayah 9 — the act of deception (khida') attributed to the Munafiqeen toward Allah and the believers.

docs.title: Important Vocabulary

docs.title: Ayah 7 — خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
docs.text: "Allah has sealed their hearts and their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment."

docs.title: The Meaning of Sealing (al-Khatm)
docs.text:
• The mufassireen explain خَتَمَ as التَّغْطِيَة (covering) and الطَّبْع (imprinting/sealing).
  • This sealing occurs as a consequence of accumulated sins: when a heart is weighed down by many sins (الذُّنُوب), the نُورُ الْبَصِيرَة (light of inner insight and Iman) becomes obscured within it.
  • The result: there is no مَسْلَك (pathway or opening) for Iman to enter the heart, and no way for kufr to exit. Kufr is locked in; Iman is locked out.

docs.title: Why Were Their Hearts Sealed?
docs.text: • Another Quranic ayah (referenced without citation) states: "Allah sealed their hearts because of their kufr (disbelief)." Thus kufr is the root cause of the sealing — the sealing is Allah's response to their persistent rejection.

docs.title: The Three Sealed Faculties
docs.text:
The sealing covers three things: 1. القلوب (Hearts) — sealed from following the truth 2. السمع (Hearing) — sealed from truly perceiving the call to guidance (دَاعِي الْفَلَاح) 3. الأبصار (Eyesight) — sealed from perceiving the نُورُ الْهِدَايَة (light of guidance)

The mufassir (referenced in text) compared all three to a sealed vessel: a container sealed on all sides from which nothing can enter and nothing can exit.

docs.title: Important Clarification
docs.text:
• This sealing is not a physical disease of the heart, ears, or eyes. Physically, these people are completely healthy and functional.
  • Despite full physical capacity, they refuse to accept the truth — as if their faculties are covered with thick veils (حُجُب كَثِيفَة).
  • This explanation employs Arabic rhetorical metaphor (majaz) to describe their spiritual condition.

docs.title: The Punishment
docs.text:
• وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ — They will have a severe and unending punishment in the hereafter.
  • Reasons: their كُفْر (disbelief), their إِجْرَام (crimes), and their تَكْذِيب بِآيَاتِ اللَّه (denial of Allah's verses).

docs.title: Al-Munasabah — Transition to the Munafiqeen Section (Ayahs 8–20)
docs.text:
The structural logic of the surah's opening is: - Ayahs 1–5: Qualities of the Mu'mineen (believers) — the righteous - Ayahs 6–7: Qualities of the Kafireen (disbelievers) — those warned or unwarned - Ayahs 8–20: Qualities of the Munafiqeen (hypocrites) — the third and most dangerous group

Allah devoted 13 full verses to the Munafiqeen — more than either other group — to highlight: 1. The great danger (خَطَر عَظِيم) they pose to the Muslim community 2. The great harm (ضَرَر كَبِير) they can inflict from within 3. Following the 13 verses, Allah gives two parables (مَثَلَان) to further clarify the nature of nifaq — to expose the inner darkness (ظُلْمَة) of their souls and the destination (مَآل) of their hypocrisy, which is destruction (هَلَاك وَدَمَار).

docs.title: Sabab al-Nuzul — Occasion of Revelation (Ayahs 8–20)
docs.text:
• Reported by Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه): these verses were revealed about the hypocrites from Ahl al-Kitab (Jews and Christians who outwardly joined the Muslim community).
  • Named leaders of the Munafiqeen:
  • Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul — the most prominent leader of the hypocrites in Madinah
  • Mu'tab ibn Qushayr — another named leader
  • Their behavior: when meeting Muslims, they would openly declare belief in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in Allah, and in the Quran — even claiming to find the Prophet's description in their own scriptures — while concealing kufr in their hearts.

docs.title: Ayah 8 — وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
docs.text: "And of the people are some who say, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but they are not believers."

docs.title: Tafseer Explanation
docs.text:
• وَمِنَ النَّاسِ فَرِيقٌ — Among people there is a group (فَرِيق)
  • يَقُولُونَ بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ — who say with their tongues (not their hearts): صَدَّقْنَا بِاللَّه — "We have affirmed belief in Allah"
  • They also claim: وَبِمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ مِنَ الْآيَاتِ الْبَيِّنَات — belief in the clear verses revealed to the Prophet ﷺ
  • They claim: وَبِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِر — belief in the Last Day, meaning the البَعْث وَالنُّشُور (resurrection and revival)
  • But Allah declares: وَمَا هُمْ عَلَى الْحَقِيقَةِ بِمُصَدِّقِينَ وَلَا مُؤْمِنِينَ — in reality, they are neither sincere affirmers nor true believers
  • The reason: لِأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ ذَلِكَ قَوْلًا دُونَ اعْتِقَاد وَكَلَامًا دُونَ تَصْدِيق — they say these words as mere speech without inner conviction, and as mere utterance without sincere belief.

docs.title: Imam al-Baydawi's Commentary
docs.text: Imam al-Baydawi describes the Munafiqeen as: - الْقِسْم الثَّالِث الْمُزَبْزَب بَيْن الْقِسْمَيْن — the third category, wavering/confused between the two groups (neither fully Mu'min nor straightforward Kafir) - They are: أَلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ — those who believed with their mouths but whose hearts did not believe - They are described as: أَخْبَث الْكَفَرَة — the most vile of all disbelievers — and أَبْغَضُهُمْ إِلَى اللَّه — the most hateful to Allah - Why? Because they mixed their kufr with خِدَاع (deception) and مَكْر (scheming/mockery of the believers) — making their disbelief more harmful and more reprehensible than open kufr. - Because of this, Allah exposed their malice and ignorance in 13 detailed verses, rebuked them, warned them, and recorded their misguidance and tyranny against them.

docs.title: Ayah 9 — يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا
docs.text:
"They [think they] deceive Allah and those who believe..."

  • يُخَادِعُونَ — from خَادَعَ يُخَادِعُ مُخَادَعَةً: to deceive, to try to trick
  • The Munafiqeen attempt to deceive Allah and deceive the Mu'mineen (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) by displaying outward Iman while hiding kufr.
  • This is the essential act of nifaq: showing belief to gain safety and belonging among Muslims while concealing their true rejection.
  • The session ended here due to prayer time; continuation scheduled for next class.

docs.title: Grammar and Language Notes
docs.text:
• خَتَمَ — Past tense (māḍī), Form I verb: خَتَمَ يَخْتِمُ خَتْمًا
  • التَّغْطِيَة — verbal noun (maṣdar) from Form II verb: غَطَّى يُغَطِّي تَغْطِيَة
  • مُصَدِّق — ism al-fā'il (active participle) from Form II: صَدَّقَ يُصَدِّقُ تَصْدِيقًا — therefore مُصَدِّق means "one who sincerely verifies/affirms"
  • صَدَّقْنَا — Form II māḍī, jamā' mutakallim (first-person plural): "we have affirmed/believed"
  • آمَنَ vs. آمَنُوا — corrected in class: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا (plural past, "those who believed"), not آمَنُوا as improperly inflected
  • آلَ يَؤُولُ — مَآل — "to lead to / result in"; مَآل is the maṣdar meaning "outcome" or "destination." The phrase وَمَا يَؤُولُ إِلَيْهِ حَالُهُمْ = "whatever their condition leads to"
  • خَادَعَ — Form III verb (mufā'alah), indicating a mutual or attempted action between two parties: يُخَادِعُونَ = "they attempt to deceive (Allah and the believers)"
  • أَخْبَث — superlative (ism tafḍīl) from خَبِيث: "most vile/wicked"
  • أَبْغَض — superlative from بَغِيض: "most hateful"

docs.title: Lessons and Practical Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Sins seal the heart progressively. Accumulated sins obscure the نُور الْبَصِيرَة (light of insight). Every sin is a layer of covering; the heart does not become sealed overnight — it is a gradual process tied directly to moral choices.

  2. Kufr is the primary cause of the seal. The sealing is Allah's response to willful and sustained rejection of truth. This should inspire fear of persistent rejection of what one knows to be true.

  3. Protect all three faculties. The heart, hearing, and sight are all mentioned together — guarding what we expose our hearts to, what we listen to, and what we look at are all equally important for preserving Iman.

  4. Supplicate consistently for a sound heart. The sheikh emphasized specific du'as:

  5. رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي — "My Lord, open my chest and ease my affair"
  6. رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّاب — "Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us; grant us mercy from Your presence — You are the Bestower."

  7. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَوَالِ نِعْمَتِكَ وَتَحَوُّلِ عَافِيَتِكَ وَفَجَاءَةِ نِقْمَتِكَ وَجَمِيعِ سَخَطِكَ — seeking refuge from the removal of blessings, the change of well-being, sudden punishment, and all causes of Allah's anger.

  8. Nifaq is worse than open kufr. The Munafiq is described as more vile and more hateful to Allah than the open disbeliever. The combination of outward Iman with inward kufr, plus deception and mockery, makes nifaq the most dangerous spiritual state.

  9. Tongue without heart is worthless. Verbal declaration of Iman (شَهَادَة بِاللِّسَان) is meaningless without تَصْدِيق بِالْقَلْب (sincere conviction of the heart). Faith must be a reality in the heart, not merely a social identity.

  10. The Muslim community must be alert to internal threats. The detailed 13-verse treatment of Munafiqeen signals that the danger from within — from those who appear to be insiders — is greater than external opposition.

docs.title: Historical Context and Stories Mentioned
docs.text:
• Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul: The foremost leader of the Munafiqeen in Madinah during the Prophet's ﷺ time. He publicly displayed Islam while actively working against the Muslim community. His name is one of the most referenced figures in the Munafiqeen context throughout Quranic tafseer.
  • Mu'tab ibn Qushayr: Another named leader of the hypocrites, mentioned by Ibn Abbas as among those about whom these ayahs were revealed.
  • Both figures represent the Munafiqeen from Ahl al-Kitab — Jews and Christians who outwardly affiliated with the Muslim community while maintaining their kufr internally.
  • Their specific tactic: telling Muslims "we find the description of your Prophet in our scriptures" — a pretense designed to appear as sincere converts while retaining their internal rejection.

docs.title: Q&A Highlights
docs.text:
Q: Does the sealing of hearts in this ayah mean a physical affliction of the heart, ears, and eyes? A: No. The sheikh clarified that these people are physically healthy and fully functional. Despite having intact hearing, sight, and cognitive ability, they see the truth and do not follow it, hear the call to guidance and do not accept it. The "sealing" is a Quranic metaphor (majaz) describing their spiritual and moral condition — not a physical disability.

Q: What is the meaning of مَآل (ma'al)? A: From آلَ يَؤُولُ — to lead to, to result in. The maṣdar مَآل means the destination or outcome of something. In context: وَمَا يَؤُولُ إِلَيْهِ حَالُهُمْ مِنَ الْهَلَاكِ وَالدَّمَار — "whatever condition of destruction their situation leads them to" — i.e., the inevitable ruin that nifaq produces.

Upcoming: Next class — two students (Atir and Fahim Mannar) assigned to read the next portion aloud. Session will continue from Ayah 9 onward.

docs.title: Tafseer 201 - Study Notes
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-20 Surah Covered: Surah Al-Baqarah (continuation) — Ayat on the Munafiqeen (Hypocrites)

docs.title: Session Overview
docs.text: This session continued the tafseer of Surah Al-Baqarah, focusing on the ayat describing the characteristics and condition of the Munafiqeen (hypocrites). The class examined the definition and types of Nifaq as explained by Imam Ibn Kathir, the interpretation of the key phrase يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ, the concept that the hypocrites ultimately only deceive themselves, the disease in their hearts (فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ), and their audacious claim to be reformers (مُصْلِحُون) when confronted about their corruption.

docs.title: Key Themes and Topics
docs.text:
1. Definition of Nifaq — Ibn Kathir's definition: إظهار الخير وإسرار الشر (showing goodness outwardly while concealing evil inwardly)
  2. Two Types of Nifaq — I'tiqadi (creedal) and 'Amali (practical/behavioral)
  3. يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ — The hypocrites' attempt to deceive Allah and the believers, and why it fails
  4. وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ — The hypocrites deceive none but themselves; the evil consequence returns to them
  5. فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا — The spiritual disease of doubt and hypocrisy, increased by Allah as a consequence of their persistence
  6. Difference between Rijs (رِجْس) and Najas (نَجَاس) — Moral versus physical impurity
  7. لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ — The charge against the Munafiqeen of spreading corruption, and their denial
  8. إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ — Their false claim of being reformers
  9. أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ — Allah's emphatic refutation using multiple rhetorical devices
  10. Why Munafiqeen are described in Madani Surahs — Nifaq as a Madinan phenomenon

docs.title: 1. Definition of Nifaq (Ibn Kathir)
docs.text:
Imam Ibn Kathir defines Nifaq as:

النِّفَاقُ هُوَ إِظْهَارُ الْخَيْرِ وَإِسْرَارُ الشَّرِّ "Nifaq is displaying goodness outwardly and concealing evil inwardly."

The Munafiq shows Islam, Iman, and all virtuous qualities externally, while concealing Kufr in the heart.

docs.title: 2. Two Types of Nifaq
docs.text:
النِّفَاق الِاعْتِقَادِي (Nifaq I'tiqadi — Creedal Hypocrisy) - Related to the 'Aqeedah (belief) itself. - The person inwardly disbelieves while outwardly claiming Islam. - Consequence: يُخَلِّدُ صَاحِبَهُ فِي النَّار — it causes its holder to remain in the Hellfire forever. - This is the most severe form of Nifaq.

النِّفَاق الْعَمَلِي (Nifaq 'Amali — Practical/Behavioral Hypocrisy) - Related to actions, not the core belief. - The person's Aqeedah is sound but their actions resemble those of hypocrites. - Consequence: مِنْ أَكْبَرِ الذُّنُوبِ وَالْأَوْزَار — it is among the greatest of major sins. - Example signs from Hadith: breaking promises, lying, betraying trust, acting treacherously in disputes.

Why Nifaq is a major sin:

لِأَنَّ الْمُنَافِقَ يُخَالِفُ قَوْلُهُ فِعْلَهُ وَسِرُّهُ عَلَى نِيَّتِهِ "Because the hypocrite's words contradict his actions, and his inner state contradicts his outer intention."

docs.title: 3. Why Descriptions of Munafiqeen Appear Only in Madani Surahs
docs.text:
وَإِنَّمَا نَزَلَتْ صِفَاتُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي السُّوَرِ الْمَدَنِيَّةِ

  • In Makkah, there was no Nifaq — the Kuffar were openly disbelievers (Kuffar and Mushrikeen).
  • No group in Makkah claimed to be Muslim while secretly hiding Kufr.
  • Nifaq as a social phenomenon arose only in Madinah, where Islam became a dominant force and some people joined outwardly for worldly benefit.
  • Therefore, all major descriptions of the Munafiqeen are found in Madani Surahs (e.g., Surah Al-Baqarah, Surah Al-Munafiqun, etc.).

docs.title: 4. يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا (Al-Baqarah 2:9)
docs.text:
Meaning: They deceive Allah and the believers.

  • يُخَادِعُونَ — from خَادَعَ يُخَادِعُ (مُفَاعَلَة form): to engage in mutual deception; here the hypocrites are the ones attempting to deceive.
  • يَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلَ الْمُخَادِع — they act as a deceiver acts.
  • بِإِظْهَارِ مَا أَظْهَرُوهُ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ — by displaying what they showed of Iman while insisting on Kufr in their hearts.

Their false belief: They thought (out of ignorance — بِجَهْلِهِمْ) that they could actually deceive Allah, just as they might deceive some believers.

Reality: وَمَا عَلِمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْدَع — "They did not know that Allah cannot be deceived," because nothing is hidden from Him.

Tarkib (Grammatical Analysis): - يُخَادِعُونَ = فِعْل - اللَّهَ = مَفْعُول بِهِ - وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا = مَعْطُوف (conjoined to مَفْعُول بِهِ); الَّذِينَ = اسم موصول; آمَنُوا = فِعْل; الضمير (هُم) = فَاعِل

docs.title: 5. وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ (Al-Baqarah 2:9)
docs.text:
Meaning: "They deceive none but themselves, and they do not perceive it."

  • لَا يَخْدَعُونَ فِي الْحَقِيقَة — in reality they are not deceiving anyone.
  • إِلَّا أَنفُسَهُم — but only themselves.
  • How? لِأَنَّ وَبَالَ فِعْلِهِمْ رَاجِعٌ عَلَيْهِمْ — because the evil consequence of their actions returns back upon them.
  • وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ — they do not perceive this reality, because of:
  • لِتَمَادِي غَفْلَتِهِمْ — their excessive heedlessness
  • وَتَكَامُلِ حَمَاقَتِهِمْ — and the completeness of their foolishness

docs.title: 6. فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا (Al-Baqarah 2:10)
docs.text:
Meaning: "In their hearts is a disease, and Allah has increased their disease."

  • The مَرَض (disease) is: شَكٌّ وَنِفَاق — doubt about Islam and hypocrisy.
  • This is a spiritual disease, not a physical one (Ibn Aslam: هَذَا الْمَرَضُ فِي الدِّين، لَا فِي الْجَسَد).
  • Allah increases their disease — فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ رِجْسًا فَوْقَ رِجْسٍ وَضَلَالًا فَوْقَ ضَلَالِهِمْ — filth upon filth, misguidance upon misguidance.
  • This increase is a consequence of their insistence on Nifaq and Kufr.
  • One interpretation (Ibn Aslam): فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا may be a du'a (prayer against them) — like the Arabic formula حَفِظَكَ اللَّه (May Allah protect you), meaning "May Allah increase their disease."

وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُون: - A painful punishment awaits them because of: 1. كَذِبُهُمْ فِي دَعْوَى الْإِيمَان — their lying in claiming Iman 2. اسْتِهْزَاؤُهُمْ بِآيَاتِ الرَّحْمَن — their mockery of the verses of Allah

docs.title: 7. Rijs (رِجْس) vs. Najas (نَجَاسَة)
docs.text: Term Type Usage رِجْس (Rijs) Moral/spiritual filth Used for idols (فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَان), Nifaq, Kufr — morally reprehensible things نَجَاسَة (Najasa) Physical impurity Ritually impure substances that affect worship

docs.title: 8. وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ (Al-Baqarah 2:11)
docs.text:
Scenario: When the believers advise the Munafiqeen: "Do not spread corruption on earth."

What is الْفَسَاد فِي الْأَرْض here?

The mufassir explains: it refers to: 1. الْكُفْر — disbelief 2. وَالْعَمَل بِالْمَعْصِيَة — all acts of disobedience to Allah 3. إِثَارَة الْفِتَن — stirring up strife and troubles 4. الصَّدّ عَن سَبِيل اللَّه — preventing people from accepting Islam

فَمَنْ عَصَى اللَّهَ فَقَدْ أَفْسَدَ فِي الْأَرْض "Whoever disobeys Allah has spread corruption on earth."

The Munafiqeen's response:

لَيْسَ شَأْنُنَا الْإِفْسَادُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَبَدًا — إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُون "Spreading corruption is not our business at all — we are only reformers!"

Imam al-Baydawi's commentary:

تَصَوَّرُوا الْفَسَادَ بِصُورَةِ الصَّلَاح لِمَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مِنَ الْمَرَض "They imagined corruption in the form of righteousness, because of the disease in their hearts."

This condition — calling evil "reform" — is a recurring phenomenon throughout history, visible in every age.

docs.title: 9. أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَكِن لَّا يَشْعُرُونَ (Al-Baqarah 2:12)
docs.text:
Allah's emphatic refutation: "Verily, indeed, it is they who are the corruptors — but they do not perceive it."

Rhetorical devices used to emphasize:

Device Function أَلَا Particle of alerting/warning (المُنَبِّه) — draws attention إِنَّ Particle of emphasis (حَرْف مُقَرِّرَة) — confirms the meaning هُمْ (pronoun Fasl) Separating pronoun between مُبْتَدَأ and خَبَر — adds additional emphasis الْمُفْسِدُونَ with أَل Making the predicate definite — further emphasis
  • Together, these four devices make this the most emphatic possible refutation in Arabic rhetorical style (أَبْلَغُ رَدٍّ).
  • وَلَكِن لَّا يَشْعُرُون — but they do not perceive it, pointing to their heedlessness and unconsciousness.

docs.title: 10. الْفِتْنَة أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْل — Brief Reference
docs.text:
The teacher referenced this concept from within Surah Al-Baqarah itself:

الْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْل — "Fitna is worse than killing."

Context: In the context of fighting between Muslims and Mushrikeen, killing is serious, but allowing the Mushrik to remain alive to spread Kufr, prevent Islam, and corrupt society is more dangerous than killing. Hence fitna (Kufr, Nifaq, strife) is graver than physical killing.

docs.title: مُفَاعَلَة Verb Form
docs.text: • خَادَعَ يُخَادِعُ مُخَادَعَةً وَخِدَاعًا — the مُفَاعَلَة (Form III) pattern in Arabic typically implies mutual action between two parties. Here the Munafiqeen are the active deceivers.

docs.title: قِيلَ — Majhool (Passive Voice)
docs.text:
• قَالَ يَقُولُ → passive: قِيلَ (it was said)
  • Used because the identity of those giving the advice is unspecified; the focus is on the advice itself.

docs.title: فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ — Two Grammatical Interpretations
docs.text:
1. Khabar (statement): Allah increased their disease as a direct consequence of their Nifaq.
  2. Du'a (supplication/imprecation): "May Allah increase their disease" — like حَفِظَكَ اللَّه.

docs.title: Key Verb Conjugations
docs.text: Root Verb Masdar Meaning خ-د-ع خَدَعَ يَخْدَعُ خِدَاع / خَدْع To deceive أ-ف-س-د أَفْسَدَ يُفْسِدُ إِفْسَاد To spread corruption أ-ص-ل-ح أَصْلَحَ يُصْلِحُ إِصْلَاح To reform خ-ل-د خَلَّدَ يُخَلِّدُ تَخْلِيد To cause to remain forever س-ع-ي سَعَى يَسْعَى سَعْي To strive, endeavor م-د-د تَمَادَى يَتَمَادَى تَمَادٍ To go too far in something

docs.title: فَصْل (Separating Pronoun)
docs.text:
When a pronoun (هُمْ) is placed between the مُبْتَدَأ and the خَبَر, it is called ضَمِير الْفَصْل. Its grammatical purpose is to emphasize restriction — confirming that the predicate belongs exclusively to that subject.

Example: أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ — "it is they (and none other) who are the corruptors."

docs.title: Lessons and Practical Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Nifaq destroys from within. The hypocrite's deception harms themselves most — وَبَالُ فِعْلِهِمْ رَاجِعٌ عَلَيْهِمْ. Every sin and deception ultimately returns to its doer.

  2. Nifaq 'Amali is a real danger for believers. When we outwardly present ourselves as practicing Muslims but privately neglect obligations (salah, truthfulness, trustworthiness), we fall into practical Nifaq — a major sin, even if not the creedal kind.

  3. Persistence in sin increases spiritual disease. The more one insists on Nifaq or Kufr, the more Allah allows their heart to harden — فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا. This is istidraj — being left to go further in error.

  4. Corruption can disguise itself as reform. The Munafiqeen called their corruption "Islah." This pattern repeats throughout history. True Muslih must align internal belief and external action; any person whose words and deeds contradict each other is exhibiting Nifaq.

  5. Heedlessness (Ghafla) is spiritually dangerous. The Munafiqeen's inability to see their own corruption was due to غَفْلَة and حَمَاقَة. Constant self-examination (muhasabah) is necessary to guard against this.

  6. Words are consequential. Lying about Iman brings عَذَاب أَلِيم. Every false claim made before Allah has weight.

  7. The Quran addresses social phenomena. Nifaq was a Madinan reality because it arose when Islam became politically significant. This teaches us that hypocrisy tends to emerge in contexts of power and social pressure — relevant to Muslim communities today.

docs.title: Historical Context and Stories Mentioned
docs.text:
• Nifaq as a Madinan phenomenon: In Makkah, opposition to Islam was open — the Kuffar and Mushrikeen made no pretense of being Muslim. The phenomenon of Nifaq emerged in Madinah after the Hijrah, when Islam became a dominant social force. Some individuals joined outwardly for political/social benefit while harboring disbelief internally. This is why all suwar describing the Munafiqeen in detail are Madani.

  • The recurring pattern of "reformers" claiming to do good while spreading corruption is noted as a timeless pattern in Muslim history and in contemporary societies — individuals and groups who call corruption "Islah" and label sincere Muslims as extremists or troublemakers.

  • الْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْل — referenced briefly in the context of the severity of Kufr and corruption over physical harm, from elsewhere in Surah Al-Baqarah.

docs.title: Q&A Highlights
docs.text:
Q: What is the difference between إِصْرَار (insisting) and إِسْرَار (concealing)?

A: These are two different words. إِصْرَار (with Sad) comes from أَصَرَّ — to insist on or persist in something, refusing to leave it. إِسْرَار (with Sin) comes from سِرٌّ (secret) — to conceal or hide something secretly. In the context of Nifaq: إِصْرَار عَلَى الْكُفْر means persisting in disbelief, while إِسْرَار الشَّرّ means concealing evil.

Q: If a Muslim habitually commits sins (e.g., missing Salah, listening to music, stealing) out of habit rather than conviction, are they a Munafiq?

A: This falls under Nifaq 'Amali (practical hypocrisy). The signs of Nifaq listed in Hadith (e.g., breaking promises, lying, betraying trust, being treacherous in disputes) relate to actions. If the person's Aqeedah is sound — they believe Islam is the truth and do not reject it — then they are not a Nifaq I'tiqadi, but their actions may carry elements of Nifaq 'Amali, which is still a major sin requiring repentance.

Q: What is the difference between رِجْس (Rijs) and نَجَاسَة (Najasa)?

A: Rijs refers to moral or spiritual filth — used in the Quran for idols (فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَان), Nifaq, and Kufr. Najasa refers to physical ritual impurity (substances that invalidate Wudu or Salah). The distinction is moral vs. physical.

Q: Is فَزَادَهُمُ اللَّهُ مَرَضًا a statement or a prayer?

A: Ibn Aslam mentions it can be read as a du'a (imprecation against them) — like saying حَفِظَكَ اللَّهُ for du'a of protection, here it would mean "May Allah increase their disease" as a consequence of their persistence. The dominant reading is as a khabar (statement of fact): Allah does increase their disease because of their insistence on Nifaq.

Q: What does اثَارَةُ الْفِتَن mean?

A: Isara means to stir up or instigate something. Fitan is the plural of Fitna — troubles, strife, trials. In the Quranic context, Fitna includes Kufr, Nifaq, and anything that causes societal chaos or turns people away from Allah. So إِثَارَةُ الْفِتَن means to actively instigate and spread Kufr, Nifaq, and social disorder.

docs.title: Tafseer 201 - Study Notes
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-25 Surah Covered: Surah Al-Baqarah — Ayat 12–16 (Munafiqeen passages)

docs.title: Session Overview
docs.text: This session continued the tafseer of the munafiqeen (hypocrites) passages in Surah Al-Baqarah, working through the textual commentary (likely from a classical tafseer text, referenced page 36 onward). The instructor explained the grammatical and rhetorical structures emphasizing the corruption of the munafiqeen, their mockery of the believers, Allah's response to their mockery, the parable of the fire, and concluded with three descriptors (deaf, dumb, blind). References were made to Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) and Ibn Katheer (رحمه الله) throughout.

docs.title: Key Themes and Topics
docs.text:
1. Inna + Hum + Al-Mufsidoon — The grammatical structure of emphasis confirming the munafiqeen are the true corruptors
  2. Lack of Iman as spiritual blindness — Their failure to perceive their own corruption stems from having no light of Iman in their hearts
  3. The munafiqeen's mockery of the Sahabah — They called believers (Bilal, Suhaib, Ammar, رضي الله عنهم) foolish and illiterate
  4. Allah's reversal — Allah restricts and limits foolishness (safaha) to the munafiqeen themselves
  5. Their double-faced behavior (nifaq and musana'ah) — Showing Iman to believers, returning to their shayateen when alone
  6. Allahu Yastahzi'u bihim — Allah's retribution mirrors their mockery in wording but is actual punishment
  7. Extending them in transgression (yamudduhum fi tughyanihim) — Allah's giving respite as a form of punishment
  8. The trade metaphor — They exchanged guidance for misguidance, a profitless transaction
  9. The parable of the fire — Their condition like one who kindles a fire, then is left in total darkness
  10. Summun Bukmun Umyun — Deaf, dumb, blind — they will not return to guidance
